title.value: All in This Together? A Preregistered Report on Deservingness of Government Aid During the COVID-19 Pandemic
title.justification: The title is explicitly stated at the beginning of the document and often repeated throughout the text.
title.quote: All in This Together? A Preregistered Report on Deservingness of Government Aid During the COVID-19 Pandemic

analysis.description: The paper investigates the public's perception of deservingness for government aid during the COVID-19 pandemic. It presents findings from a preregistered experiment that shows broad support for nondiscriminatory cash transfers in Canada, highlighting a shift towards universal and collectivist preferences during crises compared to normal times.

type.justification: The study is based on experimental evidence and surveys conducted with Canadian citizens to understand public opinion on cash transfers during COVID-19, indicating it is an empirical study.
type.quote: Using experimental evidence, we evaluate whether considerations related to deservingness, similarity, and prejudicial attitudes structure support for these transfers.

name.justification: The primary focus of the paper is on public perceptions of social welfare policies, specifically regarding cash transfers during the pandemic.
name.quote: The COVID-19 pandemic has placed unprecedented pressure on governments to engage in widespread cash transfers directly to citizens to help mitigate economic losses.

name.justification: The paper revolves around experimental surveys and analysis of public opinion regarding deservingness and support for cash transfers.
name.quote: Using experimental evidence, we evaluate whether considerations related to deservingness, similarity, and prejudicial attitudes structure support for these transfers.

name.justification: The context of the research is the COVID-19 pandemic, analyzing its impact on public attitudes towards government aid.
name.quote: The COVID-19 pandemic has placed unprecedented pressure on governments to engage in widespread cash transfers.

name.justification: The survey data used for the experiment was drawn from an online panel provided by Dynata, targeting Canadian citizens.
name.quote: A preregistered initial probe into these dynamics consisted of a survey of 2,522 Canadian citizens 18 years and older from the online panel provider Dynata.
